changes: Fixes the package repeating a short stretch of the stock OS's data (#1471).
Nothing changes in how Amiga sounds or works, and projects are not affected.
Sliced tracks stretch now: SLIC on, STRT picks the slice, and SPD and GRN stretch inside it, so a sliced loop keeps its slices at any pitch.
A cleaner stretch: every restart now crossfades over half a cycle, as Amigo's grains do, so no more ticks when PTCH goes down or SPD speeds up.
Lighter: about 64 KB less memory, and nothing is copied while a note plays at its own speed and pitch.
First release: a track machine that plays a Flex sample like an 8-bit home computer and its tracker software.
SPD sets how fast the note moves through the sample and GRN the cycle, so PTCH changes the pitch and SPD the length. STR can make it a pitch shift.
RATE is stock's own: forwards, backwards and slower, with the stretch following both ways.
On SRC SETUP: SRR lowers the storage rate, BITS the word from 16 to 4 bits, and LED adds a fixed lowpass.
Known issue: USB only, no card build. No RTRG or RTIM on an Amiga track, a sliced track is not stretched, and eight Amiga tracks at once overrun the unit (count on a few).
